SMTO-HTTP-0011 — SMTO couldn't find the web service connection it tried to use

GUID: 5863947a-27e5-42a2-a083-dbe596ab8e39
Slug: http-connection-not-found
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO tried to use a web service connection that isn't open in this task, so this request wasn't sent. This happens when the connection never finished setting up or was made in an earlier task.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to connect to the web service again and then carry on with the task. A fresh connection gives SMTO a valid link to use for the rest of this task.
  2. If an earlier step in this task showed a connection or sign-in error, fix that first, for example by correcting the saved connection in Parameter Store and selecting Test connection. SMTO can only use a connection after its setup has succeeded.
  3. Before asking SMTO to repeat a step that changes something on the service (such as creating, updating or deleting a record), check on the service whether that change already happened. A missing connection doesn't prove that earlier changes failed, and repeating them could create duplicates.

What success looks like

  • SMTO connects to the service and the next request shows a result instead of this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't assume earlier changes on the service didn't happen just because the connection was lost.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • HttpConnections.resolve rejected a connection reference that is not in the active run's registry, belongs to another owner, or was captured but never successfully established.

What this means

  • The registry is inactive, the owner differs, the reference is absent, or the referenced connection has not successfully established. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The registry is inactive, the owner differs, the reference is absent, or the referenced connection has not successfully established.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the exact reference against this run's established connections and the original connect result.

How to fix it

  • HttpConnections.resolve raises this when the registry is inactive, the owner differs, the reference is unknown, or the recipe was never marked established by a successful http.connect. Call http.connect again and use the exact connection_ref it returns; never reuse a reference from a failed connect or another run, and reconcile earlier writes before repeating them.
  • Reconnect and use the exact reference returned by a successful connection. Never guess a connection reference or reuse one from a failed connect.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended current run owns an established reference returned by successful connection setup.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
